explanation: Fires (above a quarter of max) on the word that opens a new noun-phrase slot when it is either (a) a quantity opener, meaning 'some', 'a few', 'several' or a cardinal number or year, or (b) a verb of paying, asking, presenting or receiving someone (pay, ask/asked, request, invite, welcome/welcoming, meet/meeting, present, we report, placing). Numbers, years and the weaker verbs (send, give, join, offer) cross the line mainly when they open a second clause or list item that repeats an earlier one, e.g. 'in 1987, and in 2005', '40 patients ... while 99 patients', 'take the bus, make dinner, and send'; 'some' and the strong verbs fire even alone. It stays at its floor (about 0.1 of max) on 'the', 'many', 'most', possessives, bare nouns and verbs such as find, bring, owe, provide, answer, post, see, take and make, and on a lone number or year with no earlier parallel ('enrolled 99 patients', 'grew in 2005'). Outside English prose it also fires on Polish ' z' and on the line break or heading that closes a repeated list (YAML author names, 'Sources:' items then 'References').
